request.query: A natural-number weighted reindexing of finitely supported coefficients commutes with additive homomorphisms

items.informal_name: Sum over Mapped Domain and Additive Monoid Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N]
  {f : α → β} {s : α →₀ M} (h : β → M →+ N),
  ((Finsupp.mapDomain f s).sum fun b m => (h b) m) = s.sum fun a m => (h (f a)) m
items.informal_description: For any additive commutative monoid $N$, function $f : \alpha \to \beta$, finite support function $s : \alpha \to_0 M$, and family of additive monoid homomorphisms $h : \beta \to (M \to^+ N)$, the sum of $h(b)(m)$ over the domain-mapped function $\mathrm{mapDomain}(f,s)$ equals the sum of $h(f(a))(m)$ over the original function $s$. Formally: $$\left(\sum_{b \in \mathrm{mapDomain}(f,s)} h(b)(m)\right) = \left(\sum_{a \in s} h(f(a))(m)\right).$$

items.informal_name: Commutativity of Domain and Range Mapping for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N]
  (f : α → β) (v : α →₀ M) (g : M → N) (h0 : g 0 = 0),
  (∀ (x y : M), g (x + y) = g x + g y) →
    Finsupp.mapDomain f (Finsupp.mapRange g h0 v) = Finsupp.mapRange g h0 (Finsupp.mapDomain f v)
items.informal_description: For finite support functions $\alpha \to_0 M$, if $g : M \to N$ is an additive zero-preserving map (i.e., $g(0) = 0$ and $g(x + y) = g(x) + g(y)$), then applying domain mapping followed by range mapping is equivalent to applying range mapping followed by domain mapping: $\text{mapDomain}_f(\text{mapRange}_g(v)) = \text{mapRange}_g(\text{mapDomain}_f(v))$ for any function $f : \alpha \to \beta$ and finite support function $v$.

items.informal_name: Linear Combination Commutes with Domain Mapping
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] {α' : Type u_7} {M' : Type u_8} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M']
  [inst_2 : Module R M'] {v' : α' → M'} (f : α → α') (l : α →₀ R),
  (Finsupp.linearCombination R v') (Finsupp.mapDomain f l) = (Finsupp.linearCombination R (v' ∘ f)) l
items.informal_description: For a function $ f : \alpha \to \alpha' $ and a finite support function $ l : \alpha \to_0 R $, the linear combination of the domain-mapped function $ \text{mapDomain } f \, l $ with vectors $ v' : \alpha' \to M $ equals the linear combination of $ l $ with the composed vectors $ v' \circ f $. Formally, $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } (\text{mapDomain } f \, l)} (\text{mapDomain } f \, l)(i) \cdot v'(i) = \sum_{i \in \text{support } l} l(i) \cdot v'(f(i)) $.

items.informal_name: Additive Monoid Homomorphism from Domain Mapping Equals Direct Application on Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] (f : α → β) (v : α →₀ M),
  (Finsupp.mapDomain.addMonoidHom f) v = Finsupp.mapDomain f v
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ and finite support function $ v : \alpha \to_0 M $, the additive monoid homomorphism induced by $ f $ applied to $ v $ is equal to the result of mapping the domain of $ v $ via $ f $. Formally, $ \text{mapDomain}_{f}(v) = \text{mapDomain}(f, v) $.

items.informal_name: Commutativity of Domain and Range Mapping Homomorphisms in Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N]
  (f : α → β) (g : M →+ N),
  (Finsupp.mapDomain.addMonoidHom f).comp (Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom g) =
    (Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom g).comp (Finsupp.mapDomain.addMonoidHom f)
items.informal_description: For functions $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ and $ g : M \to^+ N $, the composition of the additive monoid homomorphism induced by domain mapping $ f $ followed by range mapping $ g $ equals the composition of range mapping $ g $ followed by domain mapping $ f $. That is, $ \text{mapDomain}_f \circ \text{mapRange}_g = \text{mapRange}_g \circ \text{mapDomain}_f $ as additive monoid homomorphisms on finite support functions.

items.informal_name: Sum Preservation under Domain Mapping for Additive Homomorphisms
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N]
  {f : α → β} {s : α →₀ M} {h : β → M → N},
  (∀ (b : β), h b 0 = 0) →
    (∀ (b : β) (m₁ m₂ : M), h b (m₁ + m₂) = h b m₁ + h b m₂) →
      (Finsupp.mapDomain f s).sum h = s.sum fun a m => h (f a) m
items.informal_description: For any function $f : \alpha \to \beta$, finite support function $s : \alpha \to_0 M$, and function $h : \beta \times M \to N$ satisfying $h(b, 0) = 0$ and $h(b, m_1 + m_2) = h(b, m_1) + h(b, m_2)$ for all $b \in \beta$ and $m_1, m_2 \in M$, the sum over $\beta$ of $h(b, (\text{mapDomain } f \, s)(b))$ equals the sum over $\alpha$ of $h(f(a), s(a))$.

items.informal_name: Weighted sum of vectors indexed by σ over R
items.type:
{σ : Type u_1} →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    {R : Type u_3} → [inst : Semiring R] → (σ → M) → [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [Module R M] → (σ →₀ R) →+ M
items.informal_description: The additive homomorphism from the space of finite support functions $ \sigma \to_0 R $ to the module $ M $, which maps each finite support function $ d $ to the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} d(i) \cdot v_i $, where $ v_i $ denotes the vector associated with index $ i $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Linear Combination Map with Domain Transformation
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] {α' : Type u_7} {M' : Type u_8} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M']
  [inst_2 : Module R M'] {v' : α' → M'} (f : α → α'),
  Finsupp.linearCombination R v' ∘ₗ Finsupp.lmapDomain R R f = Finsupp.linearCombination R (v' ∘ f)
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \alpha \to \alpha' $, the composition of the linear combination map $ \text{linearCombination}_R(v') $ with the domain transformation map $ \text{Finsupp.lmapDomain}_R(f) $ equals the linear combination map $ \text{linearCombination}_R(v' \circ f) $. This establishes that transforming the domain of finite support functions via $ f $ and then taking linear combinations is equivalent to directly taking linear combinations with coefficients composed with $ f $.
